summary: Creates the Student Experience Hub product and the shared app and platform foundations through which students can navigate information, opportunities, actions and support across King’s.
detailSummary:
The Student App and Journey Integration deliverable owns the Student Experience Hub as a student-facing product and shared technical platform. It will establish the application architecture, environments, hosting, identity, navigation, interface, data and integration patterns, telemetry, assurance controls and live-service foundations needed to integrate existing systems around coherent student journeys.

The Hub will be developed iteratively. King’s Edge provides the first substantial live product demand through which the common kernel and platform patterns can be built, tested and hardened. Priority journeys and systems will then be integrated in successive phases, combining common navigation, search, personalisation, self-service and access to support while retaining authoritative source systems where appropriate.

This deliverable owns what is built and operated. The multidisciplinary staffing, product pipeline and delivery practices used to create and improve it are established through 4.1.3. Keeping those accountabilities distinct allows the app and platform roadmap, investment and service costs to be governed clearly while one team can support several product demands.

caseForChange.problem:
Students currently encounter King’s through a fragmented collection of portals, applications, websites and organisational routes. Information and functionality are structured around the systems and teams that provide them rather than around what a student is trying to achieve.

King’s also lacks a sufficiently clear shared product and platform through which those systems can be integrated. New demands can therefore create another interface, local data layer or duplicated technical capability, increasing both student effort and the long-term complexity of the digital estate.

This weakens the value of the substantial services, information and opportunities King’s already provides and makes coherent improvement harder to sustain.
caseForChange.opportunity:
The Student Experience Hub can create a common student-facing product and reusable app platform without requiring every underlying system to be replaced.

Shared foundations for identity, navigation, interface, profile, data integration, analytics, monitoring, security, accessibility and service operation can be established once and applied across different student journeys. King’s Edge can provide the first substantial live demand through which those foundations are proven before wider journeys are added.

An iterative product roadmap allows King’s to release useful journeys progressively, learn from live use and rationalise duplicated destinations only when continuity and support are assured.
caseForChange.whyNow:
King’s is at an inflection point in the future of its student-facing digital estate.

The current fragmentation is already a material source of student frustration, while King’s Edge, CRM investment and Data Foundations and Student Systems are creating immediate decisions about architecture, hosting, integration and product direction. Without a clear Hub product and platform boundary, individual programmes and services are likely to continue developing separate destinations and technical foundations that later require integration or replacement.

The full environment cannot be delivered at once, but the shared app foundations and their product and service ownership must be established now so that the Edge-led build creates reusable institutional value.
caseForChange.intendedChange:
The Student Experience Hub becomes the primary and continuously evolving student-facing product and platform for King’s.

Students can increasingly discover relevant information and opportunities, complete actions, access services and seek support through journeys designed around their needs. Existing systems continue to hold authoritative data and specialist functionality, while reusable app, integration and service capabilities allow their useful information and actions to be surfaced coherently.

The Hub has clear product, platform, investment and service ownership. Priority journeys are integrated iteratively, duplicated entry points are progressively reduced, and the multidisciplinary team established through 4.1.3 can improve the product without creating disconnected technical estates.

benefits.title: Students can navigate King’s more easily
benefits.statement: Students can find relevant information, services and actions through coherent journeys rather than identifying and navigating separate institutional systems.
benefits.realisationPeriod: From the first released priority journeys, increasing with integration
benefits.successLooksLike: Students can complete common journeys with fewer destinations, fewer dead ends and less dependence on prior institutional knowledge.

benefits.title: Access to provision becomes more equitable
benefits.statement: Personalised discovery and clearer digital routes make services and opportunities more visible to students who are less able to rely on informal knowledge, confidence or existing networks.
benefits.beneficiary: Students, particularly those currently less well served by fragmented provision
benefits.realisationPeriod: As discovery, personalisation and priority content mature
benefits.successLooksLike: Relevant provision reaches a broader range of students and differences in discovery or take-up between student groups begin to narrow.

benefits.title: King’s creates a reusable and supportable student-app platform
benefits.statement: Shared product, platform and integration capabilities reduce repeated development, support several student journeys and allow duplicated entry points to be rationalised safely.
benefits.beneficiary: Students, service owners, product teams and King’s
benefits.owner: TBC – Student Experience Hub product and platform owner
benefits.realisationPeriod: Increasing as shared components and journeys move into live use
benefits.successLooksLike: New requirements reuse the Hub’s common foundations where appropriate, live service costs and ownership are visible, and redundant portals or repeated functions can be retired without loss of necessary capability.

steps.title: Establish the shared app architecture and platform foundations
steps.summary: From November 2026 to February 2027, establish the product, architecture and technical foundations for the Student Experience Hub. Define the route from the Edge-led build into a wider student app and put in place the shared environments, hosting, release infrastructure, identity, interface, integration, observability, assurance and service patterns needed to build and operate student-facing capabilities coherently.

steps.title: Build the reusable Hub kernel through King’s Edge
steps.summary: From March to June 2027, turn the shared foundations into a reusable Hub kernel, using the replatformed King’s Edge service as the first substantial live product. Establish reusable application-shell, navigation, profile, permissions, interface, telemetry and integration capabilities without making King’s Edge a separate long-term platform.

steps.title: Prove and harden the Hub kernel through live Edge use
steps.summary: Use the 2027 King’s Edge product releases and controlled pilots to test the shared app and platform patterns under real use. Resolve weaknesses, harden reusable components, establish performance and cost evidence, and document what is ready to support the first wider student journeys.

steps.title: Approve the wider app roadmap and first non-Edge journeys
steps.summary: From March to April 2028, consolidate the Edge-focused Hub kernel, confirm which capabilities are ready for wider reuse, select the first priority student journeys beyond King’s Edge, and agree the migration, integration and product sequence for the next phase. Align the roadmap explicitly with 1.2 Data Foundations and Student Systems and the readiness of 4.1.1 Student Relationship and CRM Foundation.

steps.title: Launch the shared student app with the first non-Edge journeys
steps.summary: Turn the Edge-led environment into a common student app by introducing a shared home, navigation and profile, connecting authoritative data made available through 1.2, and releasing the first selected journeys beyond King’s Edge. Maintain authoritative source systems where appropriate while allowing students to complete useful parts of a journey within the common product.

steps.title: Expand integrated journeys and common app capabilities
steps.summary: Add further priority journeys and mature the capabilities shared across them, including common search, actions, communications, notifications, personalisation, self-service and system integration. Bring King’s Edge fully into the shared product environment and begin reducing duplicated entry points where the app can replace them safely and usefully.

steps.title: Make wider student journeys the primary product roadmap
steps.summary: Shift the centre of product demand from King’s Edge to the broader student experience. Integrate additional systems and service journeys, introduce CRM-enabled interactions as 4.1.1 becomes ready, and use common Hub capabilities to help students navigate information, opportunities, actions, progress and support through a more coherent institutional relationship.

steps.title: Consolidate the Hub and rationalise parallel entry points
steps.summary: Establish the Student Experience Hub as the primary student-facing product and platform, with enduring product ownership, platform governance, service management, cost ownership and product analytics. Progressively retire or rationalise duplicated portals and repeated functionality where continuity is assured, while retaining specialist source systems and interfaces where they continue to add necessary value.
